provenance.notes: Pro family batch. Two audiences, owners and tenants, with the owner page as the money. Fair housing applies to every rental page; copy never promises rent amounts or vacancy times. Broker licence details are bracketed placeholders. No portal or property software names.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What full property management includes, the management fee as a share of rent, leasing and renewal fees, what owners pay for maintenance, and how switching from another manager works
pageStructurePlus.why: Owners choose a property manager by comparing fees and what's included. A clear proposal page is the money page of the whole site.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Address, beds and baths, condition and availability date, and what the manager's rental analysis covers, labelled as an opinion of a rent range, not a promise
pageStructurePlus.why: Most owner conversations start with 'what would my house rent for'. An honest rental analysis request opens that conversation.

pageStructurePlus.section: Available rentals with published screening criteria
pageStructurePlus.contains: Current rental listings, written screening criteria applied the same way to every applicant, application fee, pet and assistance animal policy, and the Equal Housing Opportunity notice
pageStructurePlus.why: Tenants want to know if they qualify before paying a fee, and published criteria protect the manager under fair housing rules.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What counts as an emergency (no heat, active leak, no water), the after-hours number, a request form with photo upload, and expected response times for routine repairs
pageStructurePlus.why: Maintenance response is what tenants review and what owners ask about. A clear page cuts midnight calls about dripping taps.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Board support, meeting notices and minutes, dues collection, violations process, vendor coordination and reserve study scheduling for HOAs and small condo associations
pageStructurePlus.why: Boards are a different buyer from rental owners. A separate HOA page lets volunteer board members see the company handles associations too.

pageStructurePlus.contains: A sample monthly owner statement, what appears in the owner portal, when rent is disbursed, year-end tax forms and how reserves are held [trust account details]
pageStructurePlus.why: Owners who left a bad manager left over missing money and unclear statements. Showing the statement before signing answers that fear.

designDirections.name: Owner Enquiry
designDirections.bestFor: Small property managers with a few dozen doors who need owner enquiries, rental listings and the maintenance line working
designDirections.headlineSample: Rental property management in {City}, owners and tenants
designDirections.whyItFits: Steel blue and a plain grotesque feel like a well-run office. Two clear paths, owners and tenants, from the first screen.

designDirections.name: Owner Services Desk
designDirections.bestFor: Growing management companies winning owners from other managers, with fees, statements and services laid out for comparison
designDirections.headlineSample: Property management {City} owners can see into
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's Private Vault combo. Warm cream and an old-style serif feel like a trust office, which is what an owner handing over a rental and its rent needs to see.

designDirections.name: Neighbourhood Stewards
designDirections.bestFor: Long-standing family property management firms with HOA contracts and owner guides, selling on decades in the same neighbourhoods
designDirections.headlineSample: Managing {City} rentals and HOAs since [year founded]
designDirections.whyItFits: Brick, linen and a typewriter slab feel like a firm with filing cabinets full of history. It suits owner guides and HOA pages read slowly.

openers.line: Your Google listing has the office number but no website, so a rental owner comparing property managers can't see your fees or what management includes.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what could sit behind that button for a property manager: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your website is mostly a tenant portal login. A rental owner looking for a new property manager lands there and finds nothing written for them.
openers.hook: Open their site and check whether the home page is a login screen or a portal template. Note what an owner would see.
openers.linkLine: A property management site with an owner page up front: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website on your listing opens a Facebook page full of rental listings. Owners deciding who to trust with their property want a proposal and a sample statement, not a feed.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the latest rental they posted.

openers.line: I opened your property management site on my phone and the maintenance request form wouldn't submit. Tenants report a leak from their phone, standing in the puddle.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and try the forms. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your property management site rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way for a rental owner to ask you what their house would rent for. That question is how most owner conversations with a property manager start.
openers.hook: Check their site and profiles for a rental analysis or owner enquiry form. If there's none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A rental analysis request for owners: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your Google reviews include owners thanking you for keeping their rental full and the books clear, but those sit among tenant reviews. A property owner never sees them on your site.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase from an owner, not a tenant. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Owner reviews on the page owners actually read: {demo-link}

openers.line: Summer is when most leases turn over in {City}. A rentals page with screening criteria and online applications fills homes while you're juggling move-outs.
openers.hook: Use this from March to June. Check how they list vacancies now.
openers.linkLine: A rental listings page ready for leasing season: {demo-link}

openers.line: Tenants call the property manager at midnight about a dripping tap and a burst pipe in the same tone. A maintenance page that says what's an emergency saves the on-call phone for the real ones.
openers.hook: Call their listed number after hours. Note whether there's an emergency option.
openers.linkLine: A maintenance request and emergency line page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a leasing agent. Good candidates check whether a property management company looks organised before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the role and date.
openers.linkLine: A property management page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listings cover rentals across {City} and {Neighborhood}, but no page says where you manage. An owner in {Neighborhood} types 'property management' plus that name.
openers.hook: Map where their current rental listings are. Use the area furthest from their office.
openers.linkLine: Property management pages for each area you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: Nothing on your profile says what your property management costs. Owners expect a share of rent plus leasing fees; showing your real structure gets you on the shortlist.
openers.hook: Check every profile for fee information. If there's none, the angle holds.

openers.line: Your brokerage licence is on the state lookup, but an owner never sees it. Showing the licence, the trust account practice and the office address is what separates a property manager from a landlord with extra keys.
openers.hook: Check the state real estate licence lookup. Note that a record exists; never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence, fees and owner statements on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like most of your new owners come from realtors who sold them the rental. Even a referred owner searches your property management company before signing.
openers.hook: Look for review text or posts mentioning realtors or investors. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a referred rental owner would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts mention managing a few HOAs, but your site only talks about rentals. Volunteer board members searching for HOA management never learn you do it.
openers.hook: Only if they mention HOAs or associations anywhere. Name the type they manage.
openers.linkLine: An HOA management page for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is a well-presented rental. It deserves a listing page with screening criteria and an application, not a post that scrolls away by Friday.
openers.hook: Pick their newest rental listing post and name it exactly: neighbourhood, beds and type.
openers.linkLine: That rental, with criteria and an application: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is a well-kept rental.

I looked at property management companies in {City} and found {Business Name}, but no page that tells a rental owner your fees, what's included and what a monthly statement looks like. I put together a sample site with an owner page and a tenant side to see how it would look, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my note got buried under maintenance tickets. Here's the sample property management site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has an owner proposal page with fees, a rental analysis request, a sample owner statement, rental listings with screening criteria and a maintenance page that sorts emergencies. If it's not for you, just say so.
sequence.call:

IF NO:
"No problem. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with an owner page, a rental analysis request and a tenant maintenance page, and marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link to look at tonight?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"Your portal handles tenants. This is the part that wins owners, which is where the growth is. The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many area pages and the HOA section, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and listing updates. For a company your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, which is roughly what two new doors bring in over a year."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week?"

CLOSE:

objections.objection: My property software already gives me a website.
objections.handler: "It gives you a portal with a home page. Tenants are fine there. Owners need a proposal, fees and a sample statement, and that's the page that grows your doors."

objections.objection: We get owners from realtor referrals.
objections.handler: "Good, keep them. A referred owner still checks your property management company before signing, and a clear owner page closes that referral faster."

objections.objection: We're full. We can't take more doors.
objections.handler: "Then the site does a different job: fewer tenant calls, maintenance sorted by urgency, and a waitlist of owners you'd actually choose to take."

objections.objection: Tenant reviews are bad no matter what we do.
objections.handler: "Every property manager has that. The site puts owner reviews and your maintenance process where owners read them, and a clear emergency page cuts the angriest calls."

objections.objection: I don't want to publish our fees.
objections.handler: "You don't need exact numbers. A plain structure, management as a share of rent plus leasing fee, is enough to get on an owner's shortlist instead of being skipped."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, for the owner proposal page, rental analysis, listings with criteria and the maintenance page. That's around two new doors' fees for a year."

email.subject: Owner page for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for property management companies in {City}, and I made a sample one for {Business Name} with an owner page and a maintenance page. I'll email the link. Have a look when the tickets calm down. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} property management demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to keep it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, leasing season is a few weeks out and owners are lining up rentals for summer. You came to mind.

The property management site is still here whenever you want it, same price as before. {demo-link} if you'd like another look.

bullets: Peg the build to the yearly fees from two new doors, never to an hourly rate. Managers think in doors.
Price the owner side first; the tenant side often exists in their portal and only needs linking.
Area pages are per area, quoted only where they already manage rentals.
The HOA section is its own line; boards are a separate buyer with separate questions.
Never write a promised rent, vacancy time or 'we fill homes fast'. Rental analyses are estimates, labelled as such.
Screening criteria and fair housing notices are mandatory on every rental page, never an add-on.

whatElseYouSell.name: Rental listing photo session
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each vacant rental gets a proper photo session before listing, so it stands out among phone snapshots and the owner sees their property presented well."
whatElseYouSell.when: From the first vacancy after launch, per rental.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts for rentals and owner tips
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A weekly post on the property management Google profile, new rentals one week, an owner tip the next, so the listing looks run by people who answer."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Owner review requests at lease renewal
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When an owner's rental renews smoothly, they get a short note asking for a review. Owner reviews balance the tenant ones that every property manager gets."

whatElseYouSell.name: Quarterly rental owner newsletter
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short quarterly email to rental owners and prospects: local rental notes, a maintenance season reminder and a link to the rental analysis request."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the owner list is clean.

whatElseYouSell.name: For-rent sign and lockbox card artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "For-rent yard signs with a code to the listing and the screening criteria, so drive-by applicants land on your rental page instead of calling the office."
whatElseYouSell.when: Right after launch, before the next vacancy.

whatElseYouSell.name: Investor and realtor referral pack
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page leave-behind and a matching owner page for the realtors and investor groups who send you rental owners, with your fee structure and a sample statement."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, when they name who refers owners.

whatElseYouSell.name: Vacancy ads on Facebook
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each vacant rental gets a short ad pointing to its listing page with criteria, set up under the housing ad rules, so applicants arrive already pre-qualified."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, when they carry two or more vacancies at once.

whatElseYouSell.name: HOA resident newsletter
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A tidy newsletter for each HOA you manage, meeting dates, pool rules, dues reminders, that makes the board look organised and keeps the management contract safe."

withoutAI.route: Maintenance vendors on the approved list
withoutAI.whoPays: Each vendor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your plumbers, handymen and HVAC techs get work orders from you every week. A recommendation from the property manager who pays them is a strong door."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Vendors depend on the manager's work orders and take the manager's suggestions seriously.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The crew that turns your rentals between tenants needs a site that says 'move-out cleaning and paint for landlords'. You're their biggest client."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Turnover crews want more landlord work, and the manager's word reaches other landlords.

withoutAI.route: Realtors who sell to rental investors
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The realtors who send you investor owners need niche pages for rental property buyers. You can make the introduction in one text."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Investor-focused agents and managers refer constantly, and agents buy niche pages.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The attorney who handles your rental property disputes needs a careful site for landlords. A property manager's introduction carries weight."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Landlord attorneys get most clients from managers and value the relationship.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The agent who insures your owners' rental properties has a carrier template site. Your owners are their clients too, so you're a welcome introduction."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents and managers share the same owners and refer each other naturally.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The investor club where you speak about rental property needs a site for meetings and members. Your talk there makes you their natural recommendation."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Clubs run on volunteers and small budgets, but they buy from trusted speakers.

withAI.route: Work order photo reports for maintenance vendors
withAI.pitchLine: "Vendors on your rental work orders snap before and after shots and get a draft completion report for the property manager, with the invoice attached."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers approve invoices faster with clean reports, so vendors get paid sooner.

withAI.pitchLine: "Turnover crews get move-out photos from the rental and an assistant drafts a cleaning and paint quote by room for the crew lead to adjust."
withAI.whyItWorks: Faster quotes mean faster turnovers, which the manager and owner both want.

withAI.route: Rental deal sheets for investor realtors
withAI.pitchLine: "Realtors selling rental property get a draft deal sheet per listing: estimated rent range from the manager's data, expenses and notes, labelled as an estimate."
withAI.whyItWorks: Investor buyers want numbers fast, and the manager's rent data makes the sheet credible.

withAI.pitchLine: "Landlords who contact the attorney your property management company uses get an intake that collects lease dates and notices, with a draft summary for the attorney."
withAI.whyItWorks: Attorneys save intake time, and the manager's referrals arrive organised.

withAI.route: Landlord policy renewal drafts for insurance agents
withAI.pitchLine: "The agent insuring your rental owners can send renewal check-ins drafted per property, mentioning vacancy or renovation changes the owner reported."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents keep more landlord policies, and owners appreciate the manager-agent coordination.

withAI.route: Member question assistant for investor clubs
withAI.pitchLine: "Investor club members ask the same rental property questions every meeting. An assistant answers from the club's own talk notes, general information only, and lists local members to contact."
withAI.whyItWorks: Volunteers get their evenings back, and the property manager stays first on the member list.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back sorting owners, tenants and emergencies
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A missed call to the property management office gets a text: owner, tenant or emergency? Emergencies get the on-call number, owners get the rental analysis link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and the on-call rota.

softwareAI.name: Owner enquiry and rental analysis pipeline
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every owner enquiry from the rental analysis form on one board, from first call to signed management agreement, so no owner lead sits in someone's inbox."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their owner sales steps and who follows up.

softwareAI.name: Self-scheduled showings for vacant rentals
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants who meet the published criteria book a rental showing slot themselves, with ID confirmed first, instead of trading texts with the leasing agent."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, before leasing season. Needs their showing hours and access method.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts that never discuss a tenant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each review of the property management company gets a calm reply drafted for approval that never discusses a tenant's account or dispute in public."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their reply policy and a few approved replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Maintenance request triage assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Tenants describe the problem and upload a photo; the assistant asks the right follow-ups, marks emergencies for the on-call phone and drafts the work order for the right vendor."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their emergency rules, vendor list and work order format. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Application status texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Rental applicants get a text at each step, received, screening, decision, so the leasing office stops answering 'did you get my application'."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their application steps and portal export.

softwareAI.name: Vacancy write-ups screened for fair housing wording
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From a rental's beds, baths and features, it drafts the vacancy ad and flags phrases about who should live there before anything gets posted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs past rental ads they liked. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; staff approve every ad.

softwareAI.name: Rent comparables drafter for owner analyses
softwareAI.pitchLine: "For each rental analysis request, it pulls the company's own leased comparables nearby and drafts a rent range for the property manager to review and send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their lease history by address. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; the manager sets every range.

softwareAI.name: Lease renewal reminder sequence
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Ninety days before a lease ends, the owner gets a renewal recommendation request and the tenant gets an intent-to-renew form, on a schedule the manager sets."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs lease end dates and their renewal wording.

softwareAI.name: New owner onboarding checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A new rental owner uploads the deed, insurance, keys inventory and bank details through one checklist, and the property manager sees what's missing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their onboarding document list.

softwareAI.name: Move-in and move-out inspection app
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk each rental room by room with a phone, shots tagged to each item, and a dated inspection report goes to the owner and tenant the same day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their inspection checklist and report layout.

softwareAI.name: Move-out comparison and deposit itemisation drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It compares move-in and move-out inspection photos room by room and drafts a deposit itemisation for the property manager to check against the lease and state rules."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7, after the inspection app. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; the manager decides every deduction.

softwareAI.name: Vendor work order board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every rental work order, vendor, owner approval limit and completion photo on one board, so nobody calls three vendors to find out if the water heater got done."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their vendor list and owner approval limits.

softwareAI.name: HOA violation letter drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From a drive-by note and a photo, it drafts the HOA violation letter citing the association's own rule, for the community manager to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, if they manage HOAs. Needs each association's governing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: HOA board meeting packet builder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Agenda, financials, violation log and vendor bids for each HOA board meeting assembled into one packet, posted for the board a week ahead."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs each association's meeting calendar and report formats.

softwareAI.name: Owner monthly note drafter
softwareAI.pitchLine: "With each owner statement, a short draft note in plain words: rent collected, repairs done, anything coming up on their rental, for the property manager to edit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their statement export and tone. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Late rent reminder sequence
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Tenants get polite rent reminders before and after the due date on the schedule the lease and state rules allow, so the office only calls the real problems."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their lease terms and wording reviewed against state notice rules.

softwareAI.name: Leasing and maintenance applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for a leasing agent or maintenance tech role at the property management company answer your questions about licences, tools and on-call, and you only interview the fits."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they post a role. Needs their must-haves. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Doors and margin dashboard
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See doors under management, owner churn, vacancy days and maintenance hours per rental, so the owner of the company knows which properties are worth keeping."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9. Needs portal exports and staff time by property.

softwareAI.name: Unit turnover tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From notice to vacate through cleaning, paint, repairs, photos and listing, every rental turnover's steps and dates on one tracker."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7, before the summer leasing rush. Needs their turnover steps and vendors.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Owner proposal page as a subscription for managers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The owner proposal, fee table and rental analysis request I built for one property manager plug into any management company's existing portal site."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Most managers have a portal and no owner page, so the add-on sells without replacing anything.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member property management company an owner page template with screening criteria and fair housing notices done right."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Chapters push professional standards, and a compliant template is a benefit members use.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each property management office needs its own areas, rentals and staff under one brand. I build the owner and tenant pages once and add each office."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes many offices on the same structure.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "New rental communities need leasing sites with floor plans, criteria and tours. The property manager you built for may already be operating one."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Developers have launch budgets and want the local manager's leasing process online on day one.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Local operator pages for out-of-state rental investors
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The investment fund or investor group
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Investors buying rentals in {City} from afar need a page showing their local property manager, reporting and maintenance process to reassure their own investors."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Funds need credible local partners on paper, and the client manager is that partner.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The HOA management section I built works on its own for firms that only manage associations, with board enquiry, resident documents and meeting notices."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: HOA firms have the same board-facing needs and rarely a site that speaks to volunteers.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency signs property management companies and builds owner pages from scratch. License mine with the fee table and criteria pages already done."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the relationship; you sell them the owner-acquisition structure.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Student rental kit for landlords near campus
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Near campus, rentals lease by the bedroom on the academic calendar. A student rental site with parent guarantor forms and roommate matching fits every landlord there."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Student rentals follow one calendar, so the kit sells to every landlord at once.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Short-term rental managers need the same owner proposal and statement pages, with a guest booking side instead of tenants. Your client can introduce the ones they know."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The owner-acquisition half carries straight over, and these managers fight for owners too.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Landlord recruitment pages for housing authorities
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Housing authorities need landlords to accept vouchers. A clear page for rental owners explaining inspections, payments and contacts, built by someone who knows property management."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Authorities have outreach budgets for landlord recruitment and value a builder who speaks the owner's language.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A property manager in an open submarket
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one property management company per part of town, so owners never see my work on two competing sites. Your side of {City} is still open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Managers compete for the same owners by area, which makes exclusivity worth something.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Property managers whose site is a portal login
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Managers whose whole website is a portal login get a real owner page in front of it, without changing the portal tenants already use."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: It's an add-on, not a migration, so the decision is small and quick.

upsellLadder.line: "An owner found you through the rental analysis page. Weekly posts keep the next owner finding the property manager who looks active."

upsellLadder.offer: Owner review requests at lease renewal

upsellLadder.line: "Those renewals went well. Let's ask each rental owner for a review so owners outweigh the tenant noise."

upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of maintenance requests, and the on-call phone rings for non-emergencies.
upsellLadder.line: "The on-call phone is ringing for dripping taps. Let the assistant sort maintenance before it reaches a person."

upsellLadder.trigger: Leasing season starts with several vacancies at once.
upsellLadder.line: "Four vacancies and one leasing agent. Let qualified applicants book their own rental showings."

upsellLadder.offer: Owner enquiry and rental analysis pipeline

upsellLadder.line: "An owner enquiry slipped last week. Put every owner lead on one board until the management agreement is signed."

upsellLadder.trigger: A deposit dispute comes down to missing move-in photos.
upsellLadder.line: "That deposit dispute came down to missing photos. Dated rental inspections settle it before it starts."

upsellLadder.trigger: Their door count grows past what the owner can track by memory, at year-end planning.
upsellLadder.line: "A year of growth means some rentals cost more to manage than they pay. Let's see which ones."
